whatItDoes: Query a database on a schedule, write the narrative, render the charts, and email the report. Runs a set of read-only queries, turns each result into a metric, narrates the movement with an LLM, and renders charts in a sandbox before sending.
longDescription:
On a schedule, this queries a database, turns the numbers into a written report and a chart, and emails it — the standing "metrics email" you'd otherwise assemble by hand.

The graph is four steps: `snapshot` (database) runs a set of read-only SQL queries and turns each result into a metric — a labeled series or a single number. `narrate` (`models.run`, the live x402-served model) reads those numbers and writes a short markdown report: a summary, a few insights that cite the figures, and a line on what to watch. `chart` spins up a sandbox, renders the series into an SVG bar chart with a tiny dependency-free script, and hosts it in file storage so the report can link to it. `deliver` emails the whole thing.

Out of the box it introspects the database's own catalog — rows per table, table count, database size — so it produces a real report on any database with no setup. Point it at your own data by passing `queries` (each returns `label` and `value` columns), and at your own database by supplying `REPORT_DATABASE_URL` — read at runtime, never stored in the run. A `dryRun` reports on sample metrics and skips the send, so you can inspect the whole flow before delivery.

You pay for the database snapshot, the model that writes the narrative, and the sandbox that renders the chart, on each run — the email is cheap, and a dry run reports on sample data without touching a database.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

With no config it reports on the database's own catalog (rows per table, size), so you get a real report immediately. To report on your own data, pass `queries` — an array of `{ name, sql }` where each query returns `label` and `value` columns (a single `value` row is read as a KPI). It runs with no setup: Sapiom provisions a small Postgres and seeds a demo dataset, so the first report has real numbers in it, and the run says the data is the demo set rather than yours. To report on your own database, supply `REPORT_DATABASE_URL` or point `dbHandle` at it. Set `deliverTo` to have the report emailed; without it the report is returned in the run's output. The managed demo Postgres expires after 7 days and there is no renew verb, so a scheduled run reports when it had to provision a fresh one. Pass `dryRun: true` to report on sample metrics and get the report back without sending. To run it on a cadence, create a cron trigger on the deployed agent. The `schedule` input only records that cadence in the run output.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` to trace the whole snapshot → narrate → chart → deliver flow with Sapiom capabilities stubbed and no Sapiom capability spend; the database query and delivery are skipped. Or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.

requiredSecrets.label: Your database connection string
requiredSecrets.description: A Postgres connection string for the database to report on. Without it the report covers the seeded demo dataset instead.

settings.label: Email the report to
settings.description: Where the report is emailed. Leave it empty and the report is returned in the run's output instead.

output.subject: Database insight report
output.report:
# Database insight report

The database holds roughly 112k rows across 14 user tables and occupies 48.2 MB. Activity is concentrated in `events`, which alone accounts for the large majority of stored rows.

- `events` is by far the largest table at 81,300 rows [1]
- `users` (12,840) and `orders` (9,420) are the next largest [1]
- Total footprint is a modest 48.2 MB across 14 tables

**What to watch:** growth in `events` relative to the rest.

## Metrics
- **Rows per table (top 10):**
  - events: 81300
  - users: 12840
  - orders: 9420
  - sessions: 6110
  - invoices: 2305
- **User tables:** 14
- **Database size (MB):** 48.2

examples.title: A weekly report on your own data

queries.name: Signups per day (last 7d)
queries.sql: select to_char(created_at::date, 'Dy') as label, count(*) as value from users where created_at > now() - interval '7 days' group by 1 order by min(created_at)

queries.name: Active subscriptions
queries.sql: select count(*) as value from subscriptions where status = 'active'

zeroSetup.narrative: Snapshots the seeded demo database's own catalog, writes a real narrative report with a rendered chart, and returns it inline — nothing is emailed, because no `deliverTo` recipient is set.
